name: Eglise  De Saint Martin De Cormières
description:
It is a building with a single nave, with three bays wider than the choir, all with ribbed crossings. The general aspect of the church is that of the vaulted farms of the neighboring Causse. Its finely sculpted keystones, as well as its roof placed directly on the vault, without any framework, are original features to note.
On the outside walls, have fun noticing certain sculpted details: the coat of arms of the bishop of Rodez, a lamb... Inside, the sculptures on the keystones of the vaults will catch your eye.
tldr: Admirez l'architecture sobre et élégante de cette église rurale du Vibal, typique des fermes voûtées.

name: Eglise  Saint-Pierre de La Condomine
description: Church with a remarkable Romanesque bell tower around which nestles a small hamlet with interlocking houses
tldr: Découvrez ce village médiéval blotti autour d'un clocher roman, entre Ambialet et la nature.

name: Eglise collégiale de Salles-Curan
description: In 1452, with the agreement of Guillaume de La Tour, bishop of Rodez, the parish priest of Salles-Curan and the workers (the people responsible for the work) entrusted the construction of the new church to Dardé Alaus, a mason and renowned architect from Saint Beauzély. He is the author of the ramparts of La Couvertoirade, La Cavalerie and Sainte-Eulalie de Cernon sur le Larzac.  He kept the lease, written in langue d'Oc, to have his seigneurial chapel built on the site of the old feudal castle dating from Pépin le Bref.  In 1456, the Pope authorized the creation of a chapter or college of pri
tldr: Visitez cette collégiale du XVe siècle, joyau gothique au cœur de Salles-Curan.

name: Église d'Ayrinhac, Commune de Bertholène
description:
It was, until the end of the 19th century, a parish church before Bertholène became one.
The Romanesque church was first dedicated to Saint Julien.
The presence of the Aubrac cross above the entrance door testifies to the distant past of the Ayrinhac priory, which depended on the Aubrac dômerie.
On the south side a triangular chapel with a dome vault.
The porch, which has been enlarged and closed, houses the tombstone of a mason.
tldr: Découvrez une église romane ornée d'une croix d'Aubrac et dédiée à Saint Julien, témoin d'un passé paroissial oublié.

name: Église de Bonneterre
description:
The parish depended on the priory of Sainte Énimie en Gévaudan, to which it was given in 1104 by Abo, Lord of St Laurent dOlt. It was then reunited with the Priory of Sévérac, itself dependent on the Monastier Saint-Chaffre.
Beautiful panorama.
tldr: Visitez une église médiévale liée au prieuré de Sainte-Énimie, avec des éléments architecturaux du XIIe siècle.

name: Eglise de Bouloc
description: All that remains of this establishment is the church with its 12th century nave still covered by a 17th century roof frame, and its choir with cut-away sides from the beginning of the 15th century. The hospital organization was then transferred to the Canabières.
tldr: Admirez les vestiges d'une église du XIIe siècle, avec une charpente du XVIIe et un chœur gothique aux côtés découpés.

name: Église de Campagnac
description:
In 1895, the Romanesque church was demolished to make way for the present neo-Gothic church
The tympanum of the church, representing the martyrdom of Saint Foy, is the work of the artist Casimir Serpantié. Inside, a 17th century altarpiece with fifteen gilded medallions on an azure background depicts the mysteries of the Rosary.
tldr: Contemplez le tympan néo-gothique de Saint Foy, sculpté par Casimir Serpa, seul vestige de l'église romane disparue.

name: Église de Canet d'Olt
description: The top of the church portal is decorated with an ancient statue of St. Peter. Inside, one discovers a curious baptismal basin and the statue of St Férreol.
tldr: Observez une statue ancienne de Saint Pierre et un bassin baptismal insolite dans cette église du XIIe siècle.

name: Église de Castelnau de Mandailles
description:
The modesty of the chapel (8m X 6m) reminds us of a place of prayer reserved for the devotion of the noble ladies and families regularly residing in the castle. The overall architecture of this chapel already shows a certain elegance in the vaulting of the ridge in the pure regional style of Romanesque art. A place of worship, but also of defence, the chapel is protected by a very close archway, located below the windows, in the very corner of the tower.
The assiduous attendance of the Castelnovians at the religious services held in the seigneurial chapel made it necessary to enlarge the place
tldr: Découvrez une chapelle noble de 8m x 6m, lieu de prière discret pour les dames du château voisin.

name: EGLISE DE LA CAPELLE
description:
The hamlet of La Capelle is located on a passageway frequented in the Middle Ages, which crosses the Causse Sauveterre to Sainte-Enimie
The primitive church, which seems to date from the 12th century, was attached to the collegiate church of Saint-Martin de la Canourgue, located not far from there

The building is Romanesque: the single nave is vaulted in barrel vault with double arches that end in engaged columns
The polygonal choir, vaulted in cul-de-four, has undergone transformations that can easily be detected by paying attention to the bays of the apse: only the axial bay remains unchang
tldr: Explorez une église médiévale sur un chemin médiéval reliant le Causse Sauveterre à Sainte-Énimie.

name: Église de la Capelle Bonance
description:
Rebuilt in 1880 in the Gothic style, this church has two beautiful statues of St. Roch and the Virgin Mary as well as three 18th century paintings. It has recently been restored
The corbels of the bell tower and the modillions, under the roof, carved in stone, recall those of the Romanesque church of Estables.
tldr: Découvrez des statues du XVIIIe siècle et des corbeaux sculptés dans cette église gothique restaurée récemment.

name: Église de la Cène ou Saint-Amans
Église de La Roque-Valzergues
description: La Roque Valzergues was once a stronghold. Today, only vestiges of the old ramparts remain, with the Tour du Boulevard, the Grande Porte and its postern. The renovated old houses and the church encourage the visitor to extend his visit.
tldr: Flânez dans ce village fortifié où ne subsistent que des vestiges de remparts, une tour et une porte médiévale.

name: Eglise de Lissirou, Commune de Gaillac d'Aveyron
description:
The church was built and finished in 1849, the presbytery later in 1858. In 1875 the council of the church planned the construction of a bell tower, but this was not possible due to a lack of subsidy from the state. It was restored during the year 2000.
The parish of Lissirou was created around 1840 with a priest living there until 1918, when it was attached to the parish of Gagnac.
tldr: Visitez une église du XIXe siècle au clocher inachevé, symbole d'un projet avorté par manque de fonds.

name: Église de Malescombes
description: Inside, there are magnificent painted theatrical decorations, a remarkable stone stoup, an altarpiece that adorns the high altar, an armoured slab embedded in the floor of the seigneurial chapel and a 19th century terracotta, signed Bellegarde, in the chapel on the left.
tldr: Admirez des décors peints théâtraux, un bénitier en pierre et une dalle seigneuriale dans cette église méconnue.

name: Église de Mandailles
description:
The old castle chapel was located at the far end of the village and was built in 1802. In 1866, the present church was erected
The furniture, in neo-Gothic style, is not lacking in quality: great Christ, richly carved altar, neo-Gothic chapels
The church is dedicated to St Peter and St Martial.
tldr: Découvrez une église néo-gothique du XIXe siècle avec un mobilier de qualité et une chapelle seigneuriale.

name: EGLISE DE MONTJÉZIEU
description:
The church of Montjézieu is made of nicely dressed stones. The vaulting of the choir in cul-de-four, and that of the side chapels, in groin vault, is neat
The stones used for the triumphal arch are slightly yellow, those of the arches of the chapels clearly lighter, which gives the whole a harmonious appearance

The wooden pulpit is interesting: it is supported by a single pillar and topped by an ornamented spire with various motifs (lilies, clover). Its sides show in relief the figures of the four evangelists holding a book, which can be recognized by their attributes (lion, bull, eagle and m
tldr: Visitez une église en pierre de taille, avec des voûtes en cul-de-four et des chapelles aux croisées d'ogives soignées.

name: Église de Pierrefiche d'Olt
description:
The church is located on the edge of the plateau, on the site of what was probably the former priory. It was given to the Cistercian abbey of Bonneval (above Espalion) in 1177 by Bishop Hugues de Rodez. The abbots of Bonneval were, until the Revolution, the prioresses and lords of Pierrefiche
Around 1872, part of the church was modified in the neo-Romanesque style, and its bell tower was transformed. A recent restoration has highlighted the Romanesque choir.
tldr: Explorez une église perchée sur un plateau, ancienne dépendance de l'abbaye cistercienne de Bonneval.

name: Église de Pomayrols
description:
In the 11th century, the church of Pomayrols was donated to the Abbey of Conques which managed it until the 14th century, before handing it over to the Bishop of Rodez
In 1568, the Calvinists massacred the guards of the castle and the priests, looted the seigneurial residence, seized the treasure that the parish of St Geniez had put there for safekeeping and burnt the church and the castle.
The present building, dedicated to St Jean-Baptiste, rebuilt at the end of the 19th century, is built around the Chapel of the Rosary, also known as the Chapel of the Lords, dated 1452 and the only remnant
tldr: Découvrez une église liée à l'abbaye de Conques, marquée par les guerres de Religion et son passé médiéval.

name: EGLISE DE SAINT GERMAIN DU TEIL
description: This church is not old, it dates back to 1880, but it has a beautiful five-sided apse with five neo-Romanesque windows. On the high façade with a wide portal, there is a bell tower with three arches, topped by a fourth: it was built in 1913. The interior is vast, with its two side naves. The stone walls, the brick and plaster vault, all have been painted in bold colours: light green on the large surfaces and purple on the arches; the opposite in the apse. An original altar in Laval-du-Tarn stone adorns the choir. All this is very harmonious and successful.
tldr: Admirez une église du XIXe siècle à l'abside néo-romane et un clocher à trois arches, rare dans la région.

name: Église de Saint Laurent d'Olt
description:
Built by Jean Graffanhi, a mason from Coussergues, the church of St Laurent was then enlarged around 1860
The priory of Saint Laurent was at the time of the appointment of the Bishop of Rodez.
It contains a 1651 painting representing the crucifixion, an 18th century altarpiece (a Virgin giving the Rosary to Saint Dominic and Saint Clare) and a 15th century Pietà.
tldr: Visitez une église agrandie au XIXe siècle, liée à l'histoire du prieuré de Saint-Laurent-d'Olt.

name: Eglise de Saint-Agnan
description:
It has a portal identical to that of the church of Saint-Amans-du-Ram (commune of Vezins-de-Lévézou). The choir was built in 1440 (square vaulted chevet and cross ribbed). In a chapel, there is a Gallo-Roman sarcophagus with carved walls, representing a blacksmith's workshop. Stylistically, it cannot be dated before the 4th century.
The church was donated in 1123 by Begon de Creissels to his brothers at the monastery of Nobiliacum (St Léons). A castle built after 1592 by Antoine d Hébles to the Julien de Pégayrolles, then to the Micheau. It was used during the Revolution as a house of confinem
tldr: Découvrez un portail identique à celui de Saint-Amans-du-Ram et une galoche médiévale dans le chœur gothique.

name: Eglise de Saint-Agnan - visite groupe
description:
Guided tours of the church of St Agnan are available for groups, upon request and reservation.
Contact: Delmas Daniel on 06 86 67 20 71 - delmasdaniel@orange.fr
A listed historic monument, the church has a portal identical to that of Saint-Amans-du-Ram (Vezins-de-Lévézou). The choir was built in 1440, with a square, cross-vaulted chevet. A chapel contains a Gallo-Roman sarcophagus with sculpted walls, depicting a blacksmith's workshop. Stylistically, it cannot be dated before the 4th century.
The church was donated in 1123 by Begon de Creissels to his brothers at the monastery of Nobiliacum (S

name: Eglise de Saint-Etienne de Carcenac
description: Inside, from the destroyed former convent of the Cordeliers de Rodez, a beautiful 16th-century Piéta in polychrome stone, and the Gothic statues of the Virgin and Saint-Louis d?Aquitaine, part of an altarpiece depicting the Passion."
tldr: Découvrez une Piéta en pierre polychrome du XVIe siècle et des statues gothiques dans cette église au passé conventuel.

name: Eglise de Saint-Julien-de-Fayret
description: Composite altarpiece, medieval crucifix, carved and painted woodwork from the 18th and 19th centuries. This altarpiece and the priory chair are in the emblem of the Dominicans. Lectern with massive feet from the XVIII and XIX centuries. It is possible that they come from the Convent of Rodez, which was dependent on the Convent of Lavernhe de Séverac and therefore on the Abbey of Vabre
tldr: Admirez un retable composite et des sculptures sur bois du XVIIIe-XIXe siècle, témoins de l'art dominicain.

name: Eglise de Saint-Laurent
description:
In the 13th century, the Order of the Hospitallers of Jerusalem had possessions in Saint-Laurent, including the church. These properties had been donated towards the end of the 12th century by the Vicomte de Broquiès and other small lords. Around 1160, the original center of the Commanderie des Hospitaliers de Martrin was located in St. Laurent. The church and the nearby Hospitaller cross are the last remaining evidence of this medieval period. Rebuilt in the 15th century, the church remained a parish church until the early 19th century; the bell tower was restored in the 1990s.


The original
tldr: Visitez une église liée aux Hospitaliers de Jérusalem, fondée au XIIe siècle par un vicomte généreux.

name: Église de Saint-Victor et fresques de Nicolaï Greschny
description: From shadow towards light the scenes follow each other playing on time and space, the colours light up, attract you so that the spectacle starts. Whatever our cultural or spiritual references nobody could remain unmoved at the sacred splendour. Right next door, the Centre for Mural Art and the Interpretation of Frescos, leads you in the discovery of mural art from ancient Egypt to modern times. In Saint Victor you will also be able to contemplate the commune from the top of its watch tower (free access). Notre Dame du Désert offers a naturally exceptional site where the little train of the Ras
tldr: Plongez dans un spectacle de fresques néo-byzantines où lumière et couleurs racontent des scènes bibliques.

name: Église de Saint-Victor et fresques de Nicolaï Greschny (groupe)
description: In the Saint Victor's churche, Nicolaï Greschny shows us his treasure, 25 neo Byzantine murals that cover the whole building. The highlights of the holy story run along the arches, from shadow to light. They cover the walls to offer the fruit of that story to the visitors and to lead them to their achievement: the encounter of the human and the divine.
tldr: Découvrez 25 fresques néo-byzantines couvrant tout l'édifice, une œuvre immersive et unique en son genre.

name: Église de Sévérac l'Eglise
description: Abbé Marcellin THUBIERE, who died in 1912 and had been the parish priest since 1896, was behind the construction of the new church from 1897 to 1900, which involved demolishing the old Romanesque church on the site of today's school playground.
tldr: Explorez une église construite entre 1897 et 1900 par un curé passionné, remplaçant un ancien édifice roman.

name: Eglise de St Grégoire à Sévérac d'Aveyron
description:
This church is dedicated to Pope Gregory I. It has been classified as a Historic Monument since 1929
From the 11th century, the parish of St Gregory belongs to the Viscounty of Millau
At the end of the 11th century, it was bought by Bernard de Prévinquières, bishop of Lodève. It then belonged to one of his cousins. It is the cousin of the bishop of Prévinquières, the abbot of St Victor de Marseille, who gets the management
Around 1160, a brotherhood of St. Gregory was created and Pierre Rainal and his family donated the Mas de St. Gregory to the Chevalerie du Temple
In 1182, the church still b
tldr: Visitez une église classée Monument Historique depuis 1929, liée à la vicomté de Millau dès le XIe siècle.

name: Église de St Martin de Lenne
description:
The old texts all point out the inconvenience of this church and the continual costly and ineffective repairs. Its dilapidated state was constantly underlined. In 1739, a pastoral visit indicated that the church was in danger of falling into ruins. It was then called the Red Castle. This primitive church was also to serve as a stronghold because it had a crenellated tower with loopholes and a well inside.

It was not until Abbé Bourgade launched a serious reconstruction project in 1883. The entire population, despite the difficult times, raised the necessary funds. On 3 September 1885, the Bis
tldr: Découvrez une église dont l'état de délabrement a marqué l'histoire, avec des archives évoquant ses réparations coûteuses.

name: Eglise de St Pierre de Bessuéjouls
description:
In the nave, the two altarpieces adorning the choir and a side chapel date from the 17th and 18th centuries respectively. Access to the upper chapel, dedicated to St. Michael, is via a narrow staircase at the back of the nave (beware of the steep ascent). The chapel features a rare 12th-century altar, lintels carved with interlacing designs, figural capitals including a double-tailed mermaid flanked by two centaurs, and an interlacing capital considered a model of its kind.
To enter or leave the church, press the push-button.
tldr: Montez à la chapelle Saint-Michel par un escalier étroit et admirez les retables des XVIIe et XVIIIe siècles.

name: Église de St Saturnin de Lenne
description:
In the 11th century, Bégon de Calmont gave the churches of St Saturnin and La Roque to the Abbey of Conques. Around 1100, the monks begin the reconstruction of the building. But the work stops. The only span erected abruptly suggests for a long time that the church was built on the plans of a Greek cross.
In the course of the 13th century, the tower was completed by the construction of a bell room illuminated with 4 bays and covered with a cap topped with lauzes.
In the 14th century, the priory, along with that of Ste Eulalie dOlt, was attributed to Pierre Roger de Beaufort, future Pope Gregor
tldr: Observez une église inachevée depuis le XIIe siècle, donnée à l'abbaye de Conques par un seigneur local.

name: Eglise de St-Etienne-de-Viauresque
description:
Its decoration is inspired by that of the church of Saint-Amans-du-Ram (commune of Vezins-de-Lévézou). The chapels are 15th and 16th century. In the cemetery 2 carved crosses from the 15th and 16th century.
History and interests: Pons Stephani, bishop of Rodez, gave the church to Saint Victor of Marseille in 1082 but it later returned to the bishop's disposal.
tldr: Découvrez des chapelles du XVe-XVIe siècle et des croix sculptées dans le cimetière attenant.

name: Eglise de Verlac
description:
The church depended on the God's Chair
Built with local materials: schist for the walls, basalt, tuff and sandstone for the cut stones, it was originally composed of a simple nave finished by a dead-end vault. Two chapels with groin vaults, built later, serve as a transept. The decoration of the capitals deserves the visitor's attention. The stoneware stoup and baptismal font are probably of Romanesque origin
The interior contains a statue of St Jacques, in popular style, found in the altar building, and a beautiful statue of St Clair, in limestone, from the XV-XVIth century, coming from the c
tldr: Visitez une église construite en schiste, basalte et tuf, matériaux locaux, avec une histoire liée à la 'Chaire de Dieu'.

name: Eglise des Canabières
description: Its spandrel and font dug in an old capital in pink stone are listed in the MH. It is near the oldest hospitaller commandery of Rouergue.
tldr: Admirez une église près de la plus ancienne commanderie hospitalière du Rouergue, avec un chapiteau en pierre rose.

name: Église des Pénitents - Chapelle des Augustins
description:
The building bears the arms of Bonne de Berri, Countess of Armagnac and those of Guillemot de Solages, adviser to the Count of Armagnac. To visit it, take the door on the street side of the Town Hall
The church contains gilded wooden reliquaries, a pietà, and above all a very beautiful triptych from the 16th century, a masterpiece of flamboyant gothic art in carved wood. Attributed to itinerant Flemish artists, it represents the adoration of the Magi in its centre, circumcision and presentation in the Temple on the two painted panels. It can be seen during guided tours for groups, all year rou
tldr: Découvrez une chapelle aux armes de Bonne de Berry, avec une entrée discrète près de la mairie.

name: Eglise du XIIème siècle à Bes Bédène
description: Picturesque site, Bes Bédène is situated on a rocky granite spur set in a remarkable natural cirque. The priory was founded by Saint Gausbert in the 10th century. The Gothic style church was built in 1112. A 16th century altarpiece, statues, priestly ornaments are displayed. The bridge built in granite is a single full curve arch. This bridge assured the passage of a Roman road.
tldr: Visitez une église gothique perchée sur un éperon rocheux, dans un cirque naturel préservé depuis le Xe siècle.

name: Eglise et objets d'art précieux
description:
Since 2024, a collection of classified sacred objects has been on display in a showcase inside the church.
> Chalice and paten, Silver, 17th century. Made by Toulouse master silversmith Bertrand Lacère. Classified as a Historic Monument on December 7, 1966.
> Chalice and paten (left of display case), Vermeil, 18th century. Made by Ruthen master silversmith Jean-Joseph Lacoste. Classified as a Historic Monument on December 7, 1966.
> Processional Cross, Silver and silver-plated metal, 18th century.

> Ciborium des malades (custode), Silver, 18th century.
tldr: Découvrez des objets liturgiques classés, dont un calice et une patène en argent du XVIIe siècle, signés par un orfèvre toulousain.

name: Eglise Fortifiée d'Inières
description:
Isolated from any place of refuge, the inhabitants of this village built this surprising fortress-church in the 15th century.
As in the church of Sainte-Radegonde, its neighbor, "chambers" were built in the upper parts of the building to shelter the villagers in case of danger. A complete floor of these rooms is still visible today (access only during guided tours).
To be seen in one of the chapels of the church: a sculpted group representing the Annunciation (15th century) from the cathedral of Rodez.
tldr: Explorez une forteresse-church isolée, construite au XVe siècle pour protéger les villageois des conflits.

name: Eglise Fortifiée de Sainte Radegonde
description:
An amazing church stands in the heart of the village of Sainte-Radegonde. The building was indeed fortified from the middle of the 14th century in order to ensure the protection of the inhabitants of the place: machicolations, ramparts, stunners are still visible today.
The church has also preserved the different towers in which were built "refuge rooms" for the villagers.
To discover inside the church: a medieval fresco (end of XIIIth-beginning of XIVth century) representing the Earthly Paradise and a scene of pilgrimage in devotion to Saint Radegonde.
tldr: Visitez une église fortifiée dès le XIVe siècle, conçue pour abriter les habitants en temps de danger.

name: Eglise Notre Dame
tldr: Admirez un retable baroque monumental, classé MH, dans une église ouverte gratuitement tous les jours.

name: Eglise Notre Dame d'Aubin
description: Listed Historic Monument, this church, in addition to its harmonious architecture, seduces visitors with the treasures it houses: a Romanesque polychrome wooden Christ, a Romanesque decorated capitals, a Romanesque altar, a Gothic burial tomb... There are also traces of the 21st century with a contemporary stained glass ensemble, work of the painter Daniel Coulet and the master glass-worker Dominique Fleury.
tldr: Découvrez un Christ en bois polychrome du XIIe siècle et des chapiteaux sculptés dans cette église classée.

name: Eglise Notre Dame d'Aubin (groupes)
description: Listed Historic Monument, this church, in addition to its harmonious architecture, seduces visitors with the treasures it houses: a Romanesque polychrome wooden Christ, a Romanesque decorated capitals, a Romanesque altar, a Gothic burial tomb... There are also traces of the 21st century with a contemporary stained glass ensemble, work of the painter Daniel Coulet and the master glass-worker Dominique Fleury.

name: Eglise Notre Dame des Mines, Combes
description: Brick faced, this church's choir contains mural paintings in orange and blue tones, paying homage to the difficult work of the miners. The stained glass windows were crafted by the monks from the abbey of En Calcat. Permanent recreated display of the baby Jesus in a manger originally built in a mine gallery. Listed Historic Monument.
tldr: Admirez les fresques murales orange et bleu rendant hommage aux mineurs, et les vitraux des moines.

name: Église Notre-Dame de Lenne
description: It contains a copy of the statue of the Virgin in Majesty, from Luganhac. The original, carved in wood and dated from the 12th century, is, with that of Estables, one of the oldest in Rouergue. The statue, as well as the altarpiece of the church are classified in the inventory of historical monuments.
tldr: Voir une copie de la Vierge en Majesté du XIIe siècle, l'une des plus anciennes statues romanes de Rouergue.

name: EGLISE NOTRE-DAME DU ROSAIRE
description:
In the commune of Massegros, the village of Recoux has a pretty Romanesque church dedicated to Our Lady of the Rosary.
You enter through a porch on the south side of the building. Inside, a single nave with a barrel vault opens onto a polygonal apse with a semi-circular vault
The arcature on the sides of the apse and framing the bays is punctuated by red sandstone columns with sculpted capitals. The chevet on the outside benefits from a similar treatment.
This careful composition of the choir, as well as the barrel vaulting, are characteristic of Romanesque architecture and allow these parts o
tldr: Visitez cette église romane à nef unique, accessible par un porche sud, dans le village de Recoux.

name: Église paroissiale de St Geniez d'Olt
description:
Access to the building is via a double spiral balustered staircase. To the right of this staircase, on the site of the former grain market, is the carved portal of the N-D de Juéry Chapel (formerly located on the road to Pomayrols)
The primitive Romanesque nave (1st current span) ends in a flat chevet decorated with an altarpiece called the Olta Viel (Old Altar) with twisted columns. The painting, representing the Last Supper, was bought in Livorno in 1650.
To the right, the Chapel of the Frezals (Paul Frezals, president of the Parliament of Toulouse in the 18th century) preserves a tombstone
tldr: Montez par un escalier à double balustrade en colimaçon pour admirer le portail sculpté de la chapelle N-D de Juéry.

name: Église paroissiale Notre Dame
description:
The church was built for the parish around 1082 after the installation of the Benedictines at Saint-Michel.
The pure style of the building is an example of the sobriety and simplicity that Romanesque architecture can offer.
The paintings in the choir date from the 17th century. The angel musicians call out to us and encourage us to bring this place to life by hosting cultural events such as concerts, shows or exhibitions. For more than 10 years now, an exhibition has been organized there every summer "Notre Dame des Arts".
This church is part of a circuit dedicated to Romanesque art: "Romanesq
tldr: Découvrez une église romane sobre et pure, construite vers 1082 pour les bénédictins de Saint-Michel.

name: EGLISE PAROISSIALE SAINT-PIERRE
description:
On the Méjean causse, the hamlet of Saint-Pierre des Tripiers has a very interesting Romanesque church. Its construction was spread over several campaigns of work, which can be read on the walls inside, and give an idea of the evolution of the village
The choir is the primitive core of the church, with its narrow apse surrounded by two absiodioles, it dates from the end of the 11th century. A second campaign in the 12th century enlarged the church with the nave of three bays, then later the addition of collateral vaulted in half-barrel. The old bays above the arches can be seen on the south si
tldr: Explorez cette église romane du Méjean, dont les murs révèlent plusieurs campagnes de construction.

name: Église romane d'Estables
description:
Civilly, Estables depended on Rouergue, but spiritually, the parish belonged to the diocese of Mende, hence the name Estables de Mende. It was attached to the diocese of Rodez after the Concordat.
The church was restored in 1854. The exterior is decorated with beautifully carved modillions. Inside, it contains many historiated figurative capitals (St Michel, ...).
The Black Virgin, from the Romanesque period, from the end of the 13th century and re-gilded in the 19th century, is, with that of Lenne, among the oldest in Rouergue.
Estables was the goal of an important pilgrimage whose patron sai
tldr: Voir l'une des plus anciennes statues romanes de Rouergue, la Vierge en Majesté d'Estables.

name: Église romane de Canac
description:
Built on the site of a Gallo-Roman site and ancient necropolis, it is placed under the patronage of Saint Cyr and Saint Juliette, his mother, martyred around 303.

It was enlarged with chapels in the 14th and 15th centuries and the upper parts were redesigned in the 19th century. It is a church with an apse and apses, the southern one having disappeared.

On the outside, the cornice of the chevet is soberly decorated with alternating full and empty spaces and a succession of arches supporting limestone slate covers. To the north and south, one can observe the presence of fireplaces; to the wes
tldr: Cette église, bâtie sur une nécropole gallo-romaine, est placée sous le patronage de Saint Cyr et Sainte Juliette.

name: Eglise romane de Perse
description:
The church of Perse was the parish church of Espalion until the construction, in the 16th century, of the church of Saint-Jean-Baptiste (now the Musées des Arts et Traditions populaires and du Scaphandre) in the center of the fortified town. The Perse church was located on one of the Compostelle pilgrim routes leading from Le Puy-en-Velay to Conques.
The portal, with its monumental archivolt and tympanum, is, along with that of Conques, one of only two examples of large-scale sculptural decoration to be found in Romanesque Rouergue.
The tympanum itself illustrates the theme of Pentecost: the V
tldr: Découvrez l'ancienne église paroissiale de Perse, avant qu'elle ne devienne musée au XVIe siècle.

name: Eglise romane de Saint-Austremoine
description:
Saint-Austremoine was the original capital of the parish of Salles.

The church, dedicated to one of the evangelisers of Auvergne, was attached to Saint-Amans de Rodez.

Built in the heart of the vineyard, the building has an 11th century Romanesque transept. The chevet, the nave and the quadrangular bell tower were rebuilt in the 14th and 15th centuries. Two Romanesque chapels, with remains of frescoes, are a counterpart to the original transept.
The church has remarkable furniture.
-Majestic Romanesque Christ of the 12th century, leaning face, half-closed eyes, hair in locks on the shoulders
tldr: Visitez cette église romane dédiée à Saint Austremoine, au cœur des vignobles de Salles-la-Source.

name: Église romane de Sainte Eulalie d'Olt
description:
The building reminds, by its plan and especially its ambulatory and its oriented apses, the famous abbey church of Conques.
In the 12th century, following numerous attacks, the church was transformed into a real defense building. The interior roof was removed and the side aisles were raised. The church was reinforced with thick walls pierced with loopholes. A triforium was added to the existing ambulatory, the roof of which had previously rested on the exterior colonettes of the three chapels. During the restoration work, an altar stone from the 10th century, consecrated by Bishop Deusdet, was
tldr: Admirez l'ambulatoire et les absides orientées rappelant l'abbaye de Conques dans cette église transformée au XIIe siècle.

name: Eglise romane Saint-Blaise de Clairvaux
description: The first church and its monastery, dedicated to St Peter, were destroyed before the 11th century. The second construction dates from the second half of the 11th century but almost completely collapsed and was rebuilt in its present state between 1698 and 1704 under the authority of the monks of Conques, hence the analogies with their basilica: Romanesque church with a nave with barrel vaulting, semicircular aisles, pillars flanked by engaged pilasters, capitals with interlacing, figures of men and animals; cord and capital carvings with billet decorations. The present church is shorter than t
tldr: Découvrez les vestiges de cette église romane du XIe siècle, presque entièrement effondrée avant sa reconstruction.

name: EGLISE ROMANE SAINT-JEAN-BAPTISTE
description: Like the monastic churches, the Malène can boast of its three naves. It was probably the monks of Sainte-Enimie who built it in the 12th century. The central nave, with its barrel vaulting, divided into three bays by rectangular double doors, is supported by four enormous pillars. The semi-circular apse, with a cul-de-four, is opened through three fan-shaped windows. It is flanked by two apses, crowning the side naves. On the outside, the apse is five-sided; the arched portal dates from 1601. A chapel was added in the middle of the last century, on the north side of the building; it contains t
tldr: Visitez cette église à trois nefs, probablement construite par les moines de Sainte-Enimie au XIIe siècle.

name: Eglise romane Saint-Paul de Salles-la-Source
description:
In Salles-la-Source, in the 12th century, there were five castles and four churches.
Of the holy places, the church of Saint-Paul is the only one to have undergone neither ruin nor reconstruction. The transept, in spite of some remodeling, belongs to the 12th century. Eight capitals are decorated with different sculptures.
Among the interesting furnishings and despite the theft of several statues, we would like to point out the large 12th century crucifix preserved with its original paintings.

The church is open every day, from 10 am to 6 pm, in July, August and until mid-September.

A leafle
tldr: Voir cette église romane du XIIe siècle, la seule à n'avoir subi ni ruine ni reconstruction à Salles-la-Source.

name: Eglise romane Sainte Fauste
description: Romanesque church built in red sandstone, on the model of the abbey-church at Conques: the choir is surrounded by an ambulatory of five small chapels. Curiosity: the impression of opening upwards that the pillars give when you come into the church - a lack of verticality due to the weight of the primitive roof (the vault was covered with heavy limestone "lauzes" (roof slates) that made even heavier a thick bed of earth).
tldr: Découvrez cette église en grès rouge, inspirée de Conques, avec un chœur entouré d'un déambulatoire et cinq chapelles.

name: Église Saint Barthélémy
description: Open every day.

name: Église Saint Félix de Laissac
description:
Neo-Gothic church.
In the left apse, the baptismal font, made of the remains of an old public fountain (Griffoul), which was once on the church square.
A large painting was made in 1980 (Centenary of the Church), on the left wall of the transept by Paul Baillaud (Laissagais artist).
Hanging on the rostrum, a painting by Amand Bury (painter from Lille) which is a copy of "the apparition of the Immaculate Conception with 6 characters" by Murillo (the original is exhibited in the Louvre in Paris). Commissioned by the State in 1888.
You can also see the Cross of Boucays, at the top of the Puy-Redo
tldr: Admirez le bénitier en réemploi d'une ancienne fontaine publique et une grande peinture commémorative de 1980.

name: Eglise Saint Jean Baptiste du Poujol de CAMBOULAS
description: The castle of Camboulas, at the top of a rock in the Viaur valley, a few kilometers from Pont de Salars, the remains of the castle are witnesses to the rich history of the site in the past.
tldr: Découvrez les ruines du château de Camboulas, perché sur un rocher dominant la vallée du Viaur, vestige d'une histoire médiévale.

name: Église Saint Julien de Vimenet
description:
Several parts of this church seem to date back to the 12th century. It is believed to have been built on the site of a feudal castle chapel.
Its 14th-century bell tower served as a keep and refuge.
Between 1866 and 1869, it was enlarged between the choir and the bell tower by public subscription.
The interior features a Romanesque nave and a pentagonal Gothic choir (15th c.). An altarpiece depicts Saint Eutrope, patron saint of weavers, and Saint Roch, invoked against plague and contagious diseases. In the 21st century, 2010-2011, the town council and the parish commissioned major work to rest
tldr: Visitez cette église du XIIe siècle, ancienne chapelle castrale, où le clocher-keep servait de refuge aux villageois.

name: Église Saint Laurent de Cruéjouls
description:
The statue of St. Lawrence is placed in the Romanesque choir of the church. According to the legend, St. Lawrence died in 258, deacon of Rome, of Spanish origin, according to tradition he was burned alive on a grill for refusing to deliver the goods of the Church to the prefect of Rome, he preferred to distribute them to the poor. St. Lawrence is celebrated on August 10.
The entrance portal, originally on the south side of the church, was moved and restored in the early 19th century, using the Romanesque architecture of the time. The decorative motifs of interlacing, voussoirs and capitals are

name: Eglise Saint Martial
description:
This primitive roman church was massively rebuilt during the XII century and then fortified to face the hardships of the 100 years war. 
When you take a look at the top of the church's nave and choir, you can see the defensive hall which rests upon a crown of machicolations, all formed with arches tended between the counterforts. In the middle of these curves, you can find small bludgeons which served as a defense whether it was to control the walls or shoot with bows and crossbows. 

This remarkable curve and machicolations system could be found in many fortified castles from the XIII century
tldr: Admirez cette église romane fortifiée du XIIe siècle, témoin des conflits de la guerre de Cent Ans.

name: EGLISE SAINT MARTIN
description:
The parish church, founded as a monastery under the name of Saint Martin, became a collegiate church for lay canons in the year 1000.

The dean gave the collegiate church to the Benedictine monks of Saint-Victor de Marseille who reformed it and kept it until 1789. It is one of the most beautiful Romanesque buildings in Gévaudan.

Despite the alterations and additions of the 14th and 17th centuries, it has retained its identity and in particular its layout, characteristic of the great pilgrimage churches: a nave flanked by side aisles and an apse* with an ambulatory* onto which radiating apsidi

name: Eglise Saint Martin
description: The present structure dates from 1850, having replaced a much older and smaller church which was situated in the middle of a graveyard. Additional land was bought in 1828, thus allowing the new church to be built.

name: Église Saint Maurice d'Anglars, Commune de Bertholène
description:
Its comb belfry features two bells, the larger of which is engraved with the name of St Maurice, the parish patron saint.

The church's choir is Romanesque, while the nave and 2 chapels are Gothic.
The 16th-century portal is remarkable for its framing, and the door for its studded leaves and huge latch.
The engaged double arches rest on finely carved grotesque caps.
18th-century altarpiece.
In the right-hand chapel, the church houses a fine 16th-century tombstone, a copy of the one in Rodez Cathedral.
tldr: Église aux styles roman et gothique, avec un clocher à peigne abritant deux cloches dont une dédiée à saint Maurice.

name: Église Saint Roch de Banc, Commune de Bertholène
description:
Small, partly renovated Gothic church.
Open on request.
Used to be an annex of Anglars.
Altarpiece behind the main altar (18th) with a picturesque polychrome Virgin Mary above the tabernacle. This one dates from the 14th century, but has many Romanesque features.
In the right-hand chapel, a carved wooden altarpiece of Saint Roch. The saint and his dog are gilded, contrasting with the rest of the altarpiece, which has retained the beautiful color of the wood: the dog is admirable in its naiveté.
Old well in front of the church. At the crossroads, a carved 14th-century cross: "this is the cross
tldr: Petite église gothique ouverte sur demande, abritant un retable polychrome du XVIIIe siècle et une Vierge à l'Enfant.

name: Eglise Saint Sauveur de Grandfuel
description:
The church as it stands today dates from the 15th century. Its altarpiece and its pulpit are classified as historical monuments. The present church dates from the 15th century but its origin is much older. The primitive church is mentioned in 1079 on the site of the current presbytery.
Visit: on request by calling 06 23 98 21 14 or 06 02 34 02 57 every Sunday in July and August from 3 to 6 pm
tldr: Église du XVe siècle classée, avec un retable et une chaire à prêcher classés monuments historiques.

name: Eglise Saint-Amans
description: Initially built in the 12th century, it was entirely rebuilt in the middle of the 18th century. The church is dedicated to Saint Amans, the first evangelizing bishop of Rodez and its region. The exterior façade is in baroque style. The interior is in neo-Romanesque style. The dome is due to the painter Salinier from Rodez. The tapestries that decorate the choir date from the 16th century and relate the miracles of Saint Amans.

name: Eglise Saint-Amans-du-Ram
description:
Romanesque nave and choir (12th and 13th century). Chapels were added in the 15th and 16th centuries. Sarcophagi dug into the rock are located 200 meters behind the church.
Saint Amans du Ram, formerly Saint Amans de Uquiera (1256), depended on the manse of the chapter of Rodez. It was the seat of a community of priests

Origin: 1082 and beginning of the 12th century. The monks of the Abbey of Saint Léons (brotherhood of Saint Victor de Marseille) built a chapel in the Romanesque style on the edge of the plateau between Vialettes and Ram, under the patronage of Saint Amans. The carefully cut a
tldr: Église romane avec sarcophages creusés dans la roche à 200 mètres, liée à saint Amans, premier évêque de Rodez.

name: EGLISE SAINT-ANTOINE DU VIALA
description:
The church of Saint-Antoine, located in the hamlet of Le Viala, in the commune of Banassac-Canilhac, was built a few years after the creation of the parish in 1802.

It is representative of the new churches built in the 19th century, to which no constraint of existing buildings applied, and which present a complete and very coherent whole. The plan remains classical: it is in the form of a Latin cross with a single nave bordered by two side chapels, and ending with a rectangular apse.

But the interior is remarkable for its set of wall paintings that decorate the entire walls: the nave is cove

name: EGLISE SAINT-BARTHÉLÉMY
description:
Originally, the parish church of La Tieule, dedicated to Saint Barthélémy, was a simple rural chapel that an inscription dates from 1654. In 1808, due to the demographic and economic increase, the village was detached from the parish of Banassac and a new parish was created, which was accompanied by the construction of the church we see today.
It is composed of a single nave and two chapels near the choir. The apse is polygonal, vaulted with a pointed arch, and houses a monumental altarpiece in painted wood, composed of a central painting (a Crucifixion) of great size, framed by columns and st

name: Eglise Saint-Côme et Saint-Damien et son clocher tors
description:
The church has a "twisted" or "flamed" bell tower, with an 18-metre-high spire that turns from left to right.
The church portal features thirty sculpted medallions.
tldr: Église au clocher tors unique en Aveyron : une flèche de 18 mètres qui tourne sur elle-même, et un portail sculpté de 30 médaillons.

name: Église Saint-Fleuret
description: In Gothic style, it is endowed with rich ornaments, notably six altarpieces from the 17th and 18th centuries bearing gilded wooden statues, paintings and bas-reliefs - a collection of procession sticks from the Brotherhood of the Blue Penitents - the relics of Saint Fleuret, patron saint of Estaing- the contemporary stained glass windows of Claude Baillon.
tldr: Église gothique ornée de six retables baroques, statues dorées et bas-reliefs, dont une collection de bâtons de procession.

name: Église Saint-Jacques le Majeur
description: Dating from the 15th century, this church was built by the will of Jean III d'Arpajon and his wife Anne de Bourbon Roussillon, Lords of the Brousse. Located below the castle, it can be reached by about twenty steps, most of which are under the vault of a tower that serves as a bell tower. In 2000 a truly exemplary restoration of the monument revealed the traces of an old fresco dating from the 15th century as well as beautiful elements of typically Gothic sculptures. The cemetery and the adjoining oratory date from the same period.
tldr: Église du XVe siècle construite par les seigneurs de Brousse, accessible par un sentier depuis le château médiéval.

name: EGLISE SAINT-MARTIN
description:
The church of Massegros is a recent church built between 1912 and 1914

Its construction is neat: the plan is composed of a central nave with its two side aisles. The square bell tower is topped by a statue of Saint-Privat, which can be seen from afar. The exterior of the building has ashlar frames and corners alternating with light-coloured plaster

The central vault is a pointed arch and the side chapels are cross-vaulted, all covered with orange plaster
The whole is slender and luminous, and numerous stained glass windows with stories decorate the side bays.  Representing the Virgin Mary, S

name: EGLISE SAINT-MARTIN D'AUXILLAC
description:
The church has a Latin cross plan with three bays with barrel vaults and two side chapels
The interior is entirely covered with wall paintings in good condition, which date from 1921. Indeed, it was at this date that the state of the church was judged to be in a bad state, and that major work was undertaken, under the impetus of the mayor of Auxillac and bishop of Rodez, Charles de Ligonnès
The walls, the vault of the nave and the arches of the chapels were painted in faux-apparatus, and draperies appeared on the sides of the circular apse and on the walls of the chapels. On the apse's cul-de-
tldr: Église aux fresques murales de 1921 couvrant entièrement l'intérieur, dans un style sobre et élégant.

name: EGLISE SAINT-MARTIN DE PIN
description:
Donated to the monastery of Chirac by Aldebert II of Peyre in the early 12th century, the church, set in a charming location, is still surrounded byof its cemetery, which contains steles of archaeological interest (some from the Merovingian period), making this an exceptional heritage site. 
TheRomanesque building features a five-sided apse and consists of a single nave, two side chapels forming a false transept, a north side chapel beneath the bell tower, and a sacristy attached to the south of the chancel. 
The %E9church was %E9xtensively remodeled %E0 during the %E9Gothic period, from which
tldr: Église du XIIe siècle entourée de stèles archéologiques, offerte au monastère de Chirac par les seigneurs locaux.

name: Eglise Saint-Martin des Faux
description:
Church open to the public (subject to reservation) every day in July-August and on weekends from April to June. Historical details in the building.
The church contains a 17th century altarpiece at the high altar and statues of bishops. A second altarpiece is dedicated to the Virgin. The parish had as an annex the chapel of Saint-Hippolyte, which was destroyed a long time ago in place of the present statue of the Virgin near the cemetery. An ancient sarcophagus can also be seen in the cemetery. In the village, a rustic monument to the dead, made of 3 large stones, pays homage to 3 men of the pa
tldr: Église ouverte en été, abritant un retable du XVIIe siècle et des détails historiques à découvrir sur réservation.

name: EGLISE SAINT-MEDARD DE BANASSAC
description:
The church of Saint-Médard de Banassac is mentioned as early as 1123 among the possessions of the chapter of Mende, but the eventful history of the territory, in particular the wars of Religions, has led to many changes. In 1591, multiple degradations were reported and works were ordered in the 17th century
In addition to repairing the vaults, the latter consisted of the construction of a three-bay south side aisle, in order to complete the building which, originally, had only one vessel. The side aisle leads to the Chapel of the Virgin, which has Gothic features.
The polygonal vaulted choir h
tldr: Découvrez une église médiévale aux pierres rouges, témoin des guerres de Religion et de l’histoire locale.

name: EGLISE SAINT-PIERRE-ET-SAINT-PAUL
description:
Since the Middle Ages and until the French Revolution, this village was part of the mandement of Nogaret. This territorial subdivision included all the villages and hamlets of this part of the territory, made of multiple valleys between the Lot and the Aubrac plateau

The parish church of Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul stands in the middle of the village of Saint-Pierre-de-Nogaret. The use of red sandstone for the construction of a large part of the building gives it this particular colour
The church is accessed from the south side, along the cemetery, which also offers a nice view of the surround
tldr: Visitez une église médiévale nichée dans un village chargé d’histoire, ancienne possession des Nogaret.

name: EGLISE SAINT-PRÉJET
description:
Saint-Préjet du Tarn is a Romanesque church overlooking the Tarn. It is the former parish church of the hamlet of Saint-Préjet, which was located opposite that of Les Vignes. Its first mention dates from 1155 but its construction is probably earlier. The monks of the monastery of Rozier seem to have played an important role in its construction
Saint-Préjet has preserved its Romanesque character through the general structure of the building (a single nave opening onto a three-sided apse decorated with an arcature, surrounded by two apsidioles) and through the barrel vaulting
On the outside too,
tldr: Admirez une église romane perchée au-dessus du Tarn, avec son chevet roman et son cadre sauvage.

name: EGLISE SAINT-PRIVAT
description:
The church of Combret, built in 1843, is dedicated to Saint Privat.
Its characteristic roof, in the shape of an overturned ship's hull (the so-called "Philibert" roof) is the first remarkable feature of the building
Its simple plan is composed of a single nave of two bays completed by two side chapels near the choir.
Inside, the decoration of the church is composed of a beautiful set of furniture containing statues and paintings that decorate it nicely, especially the painting on the left which represents a martyr recognizable by her palm
The choir benefits from a monumental treatment, with in
tldr: Émerveillez-vous devant une église au toit en forme de coque de bateau, unique en son genre.

name: EGLISE SAINT-SAUVEUR
description:
It's a monastic church, built by the monks from Aniane. If the vault has been redone and the walls rebuilt, the chevet and chapel have escaped the devastation of the wars of religion and date back to the 12th century.
This church is rather surprising, by the columns, three on one side and three on the other, which separate the nave from the side aisles; built in rough stone, now exposed, these bitter columns without base nor crown make the sharpest contrast with the slender columns of the seven arcades of the apse.
tldr: Explorez une église monastique du IXe siècle, l’une des rares à avoir résisté aux guerres de Religion.

name: EGLISE SAINT-VINCENT DE CANILHAC
description:
The parish church is reached by crossing the enclosed cemetery that surrounds it, then passing under the porch that precedes the entrance
It is a church built in limestone and red sandstone for the corners. This sandstone, with its particular colour, is characteristic of the Banassac area
The building is built in a very marked Romanesque style: the central nave and the side aisles are vaulted in full barrel, the pillars are massive and the bays narrow. The double arches of the central nave stand out because they are made of red sandstone
The oldest part is mainly made up of the choir and the a
tldr: Traversez un cimetière clos pour accéder à une église en pierre ocre et grès rouge, typique du Gévaudan.

name: Eglise Sainte Croix
description: Confirmed since 1147, this church kept its place at the border of the sauveté and played a great role in the defense system. The Sainte-Croix church was first and foremost a roman church. From that era subsists the nef which kept its pillars and dimensions. Changes were operated during the XVIth and the XVIIth century with the vaults and the contruction of a bell tower. The church was then extended by the opening of the side aisles and the creation of the west door in 1865-1868. Finally, in 1896-1898, the last work were finalized : the erection of the bell tower and the reconstruction of the r
tldr: Découvrez une église-forteresse du XIIe siècle, gardienne d’une sauveté médiévale et de son système défensif.

name: Eglise Sainte Madeleine
description:
Built in the 15th century by Lord Alzias de Saunhac, the church is home to his tomb, decorated with a remarkable recumbent statue.
The church features the Saunhac family coat of arms, a statue of Saint Christophe and four statues listed as historic monuments.
A contemporary Stations of the Cross by Casimir Ferrer is also on display.
tldr: Contemplez le tombeau sculpté d’un seigneur du XVe siècle et des blasons familiaux dans une église gothique.

name: EGLISE SAINTE-MADELEINE
description:
The choir of the church of Les Hermaux, which is the oldest part of the building, was the chapel of a castle dating from the 12th century, now disappeared. The five-sided Romanesque apse is divided into two floors, underlined by a cornice set on a row of billets. The semi-circular arches fall on high embedded columns
With the north chapel, which has also preserved its stonework, the choir is the oldest and most remarkable part
The massive bell tower, topped by a slender spire, was built in the 19th century.
tldr: Visitez une église romane du XIIe siècle, ancienne chapelle castrale aux cinq pans et sculptures anciennes.

name: EGLISE St Amans de Salmiech
description: Dedicated to Saint-Amans, the church of the Aveyron commune of Salmiech is located on the western edge of the Lévézou plateau. A composite building marked by the end of the flamboyant Gothic and Renaissance styles (15th-16th centuries), the original foundation seems to have been undertaken in the 5th century under the episcopate of the first bishop of Rodez; it was therefore placed under the name of "Saint-Amans". The whole monument appears rectangular, in extension of the bell tower and the base of the church where a sacristy is built and replaces the entrance hatch. The nave is made up of 4
tldr: Admirez une église composite mêlant gothique flamboyant et Renaissance, perchée sur le plateau du Lévézou.

name: Église St Cyrice et Ste Juliette de Montjaux
description:
Open all year round on request, contact the Town Hall

The church of Saint-Cyrice-et-Sainte-Juliette is a catholic church classified as a historical monument for the remarkable Romanesque vestiges that it preserves.
This church is part of a discovery circuit dedicated to Romanesque art: "Romanesque heritage along the valleys of the Muse, the Rasp of the Tarn and surroundings"


When, from the high plateaus of Lévézou, the traveler's gaze is directed towards the valley of the Tarn, there is a great chance that he will pass by Montjaux via the D999

This small town, clinging to the south-eastern
tldr: Découvrez des vestiges romans classés, dans une église ouverte sur demande au cœur de l’Aveyron.

name: Église St Jacques de Salsac
description:
In the heart of the Regional Natural Park of the Grands Causses, the church of Saint Jacques de Salsac is located in the valley of the Muse, on the territory of the Aveyron commune of Saint Beauzély. This monument is a pre-Romanesque as well as Romanesque building from the 10th and 12th centuries, built of sandstone and covered with schist slates. Probably built on the bases of a Gallo-Roman villa located at the edge of an old road connecting the Roman way of Millau to Rodez via Ségur, this church is equipped with architectural details of quality: vault in full arch, fragments of paintings..
I
tldr: Trouvez une église médiévale blottie dans la vallée de la Muse, au cœur du Parc des Grands Causses.

name: Eglise St Jean-Baptiste de La Bastide l'Evêque
description:
The church's most ancient parts are the pentagonal choir and the arms of the transept. The grayish stained glass is also quite ancient, dating back to the end of the Middle Age. It is decorated with a rare crucifixion.
Both lateral chapels extended the church during the XVIth century. The north one is dedicated to the Virgin whilst the south one is placed under the patronage of St Dalmas. He is represented in a gold reliquary bust and a pilgrimage was also dedicated to him. 

The steeple porch was in all likelyhood built during the XVIth century. It crosses the street which reminds us of the V
tldr: Observez des vitraux médiévaux et un chœur pentagonal dans cette église aux origines anciennes.

name: Église St Laurent de Prades d'Aubrac
description:
Father André proceeds with the reconstruction of the church. Disappointed by the reception given to his work, he had an inscription placed under the porch: "It is difficult to do something that is to everyone's taste". He died in the Château de Salle on 16 May 1546.
The church, completed by his successor Georges d'Armagnac, is one of the few in Rouergue to have hanging keystones. Mixing Gothic and Renaissance styles, it is among the most remarkable in Rouergue and deserves a careful visit.
Above the porch is a 15th century pietà made of polychrome stone.
Inside, the pulpit, composed of 6 stone
tldr: Visitez une église en reconstruction, marquée par une inscription touchante du père André.

name: Église St-Michel
description:
In the years 1070-1082, Jean Langobard rebuilt the church founded by Bernard de Lévézou on an ancient place of worship for the abbey of Marseille in order to establish a Benedictine monastery.
The Romanesque architecture is characterized by a robust, severe aspect and a great harmony of proportions.
By its height, its sobriety, its luminosity and its acoustics, the building illustrates the rigour of monastic churches. The crypt under the choir houses a spring, a silent witness to a distant past that still holds many secrets today.
Still in activity, the church of Saint Michel is the parish chu
tldr: Explorez une église bénédictine du XIe siècle, fondée sur un lieu de culte antique près de Millau.

name: Église St-Sauveur
description:
Located in the Parc Naturel Régional des Grands Causses, the southern Aveyron village of Verrières boasts the ruins of an old castle and three religious buildings.

Dedicated to Saint Sauveur, the village church dates back to the 11th century, but was remodeled in the 16th century following the Protestant siege of Verrières. Featuring circular pillars supporting the vaults, as well as paired and superimposed columns to mark the entrance to the choir, this monument boasts architectural elements characteristic of regional Romanesque art. Partly ruined in the 19th century, restoration programs we
tldr: Découvrez les ruines d’un château et une église dédiée à Saint-Sauveur, en plein cœur des Grands Causses.

name: Eglise Ste-Thérèse à Durenque
description: Free visit, the church is open every day from 9:30 am to 6 pm.
tldr: Passez devant une église moderne dédiée à Sainte-Thérèse, accessible librement toute l’année.

name: El Colibri
tldr: Visitez une ancienne usine reconvertie en lieu culturel insolite, dédié à l’art et à la mémoire locale.

name: ELEVAGE RODIER
description:
We cultivate, we breed, we share.
Come and meet our Aubrac cows, our Alpine goats and our farm pigs, discover our history and our production methods, enjoy our products...
Family breeding carried out in reasoned agriculture for healthy and quality products: meat, cooked pork meats, cheeses, ready-made meals...
Many events throughout the year, go to the facebook page Elevage Rodier Sartre to learn more.
Live a moment of sharing around big friendly boards. in the restaurant of the breeding!
tldr: Rencontrez vaches Aubrac et chèvres des Alpes, dégustez leurs produits fermiers dans un cadre authentique.

name: Elo'Distille
description:
A distiller based in Bournac near Saint-Affrique, Elodie offers 100% local essential oils, balms, vegetable oils and floral waters
A professional alembic maker, she is involved in every stage of the process, making all her products from "plant to bottle".
You can find all her products at the L'Effet des mains boutique and the Epicerie del Pais in Saint-Affrique.
The stores are open from Tuesday to Saturday.
tldr: Découvrez des huiles essentielles 100% locales et des savoir-faire d'alambic dans un atelier artisanal.

name: ELSA Base Canoë-kayak Espalion
description:
Discover a preserved environment classified Natura 2000 by canoe. Our canoe trips take you through some of France's most beautiful villages, and promise great fun for families and friends for half a day or a whole day! Able to swim from age 6.
Special St-Jacques canoe-kayak: Give your feet a break and go light! We'll carry your backpacks!
Saint-Côme / Estaing (17km) or Espalion / Estaing (12km)
tldr: Pagayez dans les gorges du Tarn, classées Natura 2000, entre villages pittoresques et nature préservée.

name: ELSA Base Canoë-kayak Espalion - Descente spéciale Saint-Jacques
description: Three possible routes: Saint-Come / Espalion (5km) - Saint-Côme / Estaing (17km) or Espalion / Estaing (12km). We'll carry your bags and hand them over to you on arrival.
tldr: Descendez l'Aveyron en canoë avec transport de bagages inclus, entre Saint-Côme et Estaing.

name: ELSA Location Canoë-Paddle Estaing
description:
Discover the village of Estaing, classified as "France's most beautiful village", by Stand Up Paddle or canoe. In a preserved environment classified Natura 2000, our rentals on the Golinhac reservoir promise great moments to enjoy with family or friends for an hour or half a day! From age 6, swimming ability required.
Every Wednesday of the season at 8pm, we also offer a 1h30 initiation to Stand Up Paddle at dusk on the Estaing lake. Come and discover Estaing and its village, classified as "France's most beautiful village", in an unusual way. Take advantage of the aperitif offered at the end o
tldr: Explorez le village d'Estaing en paddle ou canoë sur le lac de Golinhac, classé Natura 2000.

name: Emilie Séguret - Vitrailliste
description:
Whether it's restoration or creation, I love working with glass for its colors, but also for its history. As a stained glass artist and rope access technician, I'm not afraid of heights, and can work without scaffolding on high-flying sites. I can create large or small decorative or practical pieces.
Interested?
You can find my creations at the "Le mouton dans l'herbe" store in Marcillac-Vallon.
tldr: Admirez ou restaurez des vitraux, même en hauteur, avec une artiste passionnée et acrobate.

name: Emotion Canoë
description:
Course "Emotion" (The Unforgettable): Les Vignes - St-Pal, about 11km
Course "promenade" : St-Pal  - Peyrelade

name: Établissement rural du haut moyen age : les Aouzéras
ETANG DE BONNECOMBE
description:
The Bonnecombe Pond is located in the canton of Saint-Germain-du-Teil, near the town of Les Salces, below the Bonnecombe Pass.

At an altitude of 1,350 meters in the Aubrac region, the pond is an ideal spot for fishing for rainbow trout.

Several docks have been installed to provide easy access during a walk around the pond. However, the setting remains wild enough to observe the local flora and fauna.

The site is accessible year-round. The fishing pond is open for fishing from May 1, 2026, to June 30, 2026, on weekends and holidays. From July 1, 2026, to September 14, 2026, it is open daily.
tldr: Baladez-vous autour d’un étang de montagne à 1350 m d’altitude, idéal pour une pause nature en Aubrac.

name: Etang de l'oeil bleu

According to the legend, a troubadour charmed a young girl with pure blue eyes by his songs listened every evening around the pond. After he left, she finally saw his face on the surface of the water and went to join him. One morning they noticed that the water of the pond was clearer and bluer and the beautiful mourning girl was never seen again.
tldr: Détendez-vous au bord d’un étang légendaire, où un troubadour aurait séduit une jeune fille aux yeux bleus.

tldr: Parcourez les Grands Causses et les Cévennes à pied, guidé par des passionnés pour en découvrir les secrets.

tldr: Survolez les Grands Causses en parapente avec une école professionnelle depuis 1985, pour une vue imprenable.

tldr: Offrez-vous une parenthèse bien-être avec massages tantriques ou énergétiques dans un centre dédié.

name: Explore Baraqueville
description:
Today, the Val de Lenne Lake with its amenities is the first tourist attraction in Baraqueville, prized by visitors as well as the inhabitants : several bike and foot trails, a beach (bathing supervised in summer), summer watersports (pedalo, stand-up paddle, canoe)... The ideal place to relax and have a picnic. In a word : "enjoy"!
A crossroads...
All starts around 1749. At that time, Intendant Lescalopier decided to make the 3rd and 5th Royal Roads cross where Baraqueville would appear later. The site was 1st called "Crossroads of the Albi way", until 1810 when was built the relay station "L
tldr: Profitez des sentiers pédestres et du lac de la Val de Lenne, idéal pour une balade en famille ou un pique-nique.

name: Explore Boussac
description:
A church firmly planted on the ground...


Built during 13th century, then fortified by the inhabitants during 14th & 15th centuries in order to protect themselves from the English invasion, its base gives evidence of it, with its 1 metre thick!

Also, crenels & arrow-loops & machicolation witness this defensive purpose. 3 storeys with rooms & accommodations were fit out above the nave in anticipation of prolonged sieges.
Enter the church, admire the strength of its pillars, peer into the magnificent golden altarpiece to identify the various figures represented... & try to locate the pipe inte
tldr: Découvrez une église fortifiée du XIIIe siècle, symbole de résistance face aux invasions anglaises.

name: Explore Calmont - fortified village
description:
Its 15th century keep - private property -: this is all what remains of the castle of Calmont-de-Plancatge, former fief of the Arpajons, a barony who played an important role in the region's life. 


Renowened in the past for its fairs & hemp growing, now the village distinguishes itself thanks to its old half-timbered houses dating back to 15th century. A walk in the alleys will be enough for you to fell under its spell...

You want to go for a bike ride? Pedal along the itinerary "Le Tour des 5 clochers" - description in French - that will give you the opportunity to discover the unmissable
tldr: Visitez les vestiges d'un château médiéval du XVe siècle, dernier témoin d'une baronnie influente de la région.

name: Explore Castelmary - fortified area
description:
More than 1,000 years of history...


Named Castrum Marinum in Latin, the hamlet's history can be dated back to 10th century, most probably.
Its nature defences - dense forest, steep land & rocks - & its geographical location - at the gates of the Rouergue region - explain its major military role : remains of the Castelmary Castle still testify to the important role played by this village in the Middle Age.

Owned by the Castelmaries from 11th to 14th century, this place was occupied by several Lords until the last ones : the Puel de Parlan family. These viscounts had bought the barony for exa
tldr: Explorez un hameau fortifié vieux de plus de 1000 ans, protégé par une forêt dense et des reliefs escarpés.

name: Explore Castelpers
description:
A moving castle...
Its first castle, built during mid-11th century, is the siege of powerful lords, who rule the area until the crusades era. When the Rouergue is dismantled, the Castelpers Lordship becomes one of the 12 baronies of the Rodez County.
After the 15th-century English occupation and the plunders led by bands of "routiers" (bandits), Castelpers endures the Wars of Religion, Lord Jean de Castelpers being the Calvinist Party leader.
Partially destroyed, deserted by its inhabitants, the old castle settled on the rocky spur overlooking the valley, is used as a quarry to buid the presen
tldr: Découvrez un château médiéval chargé d'histoire, témoin des croisades et des seigneurs puissants du Rouergue.

name: Explore Gramond
description:
The first thing you notice when arriving in Gramond is the large 3-wing building, formerly house of the Domican Sisters, a congregation founded in 1843. Nowadays, it has become a retirement home.
Close by, in the inner village, stands a magnificent oratory - classified as a historical monument - that shelters a Pieta, masterpiece of the 16th-century sculpture. It depicts a Virgin hugging Christ's arm, with Saint John and Saint Magdalena by her side.
Nearby, waits for you Ceres, Goddess of the Harvest, a sculpture made by Paul Belmondo (1898-1982). This sculptor is considered as one of the most
tldr: Visitez l'ancien couvent des Dominicaines, devenu maison de retraite, et son architecture imposante du XIXe siècle.

name: Explore Naucelle
description:
To enter this town founded by Cistercian monks during the 12th century, use the Englishmen's Door, classified as an historical monument. Visit Saint-Martin Church with its magnificent organ and, once arrived in rue du Four, look up to admire the half-timbered houses.


What is a “sauveté”? In short: a place where you are safe (“sauf” in French)! 
It was a village or a market town built on seigneurial lands, around a church and its priory. Its territorial boundaries were shown thanks to stone crosses. The inhabitants benefited from a spiritual protection and a plot on which they could build fre
tldr: Passez la porte des Anglais, classée monument historique, et admirez l'église Saint-Martin et son orgue remarquable.

name: Explore Sauveterre de Rouergue
description:
Enter through the Saint-Christophe fortified gate and walk the Medieval alleys. They will drive you to the central square with its 47 arches surrounded by covered passageways. There, are gathered the big and beautiful houses that were owned by shopkeepers, magistrates and other prominent citizens. Prolong your immersive experience with a gourmet break.


What is a “bastide”?

It is a new town built between the 13th and the early 14th centuries. Its map is regular and distributed around a central square. It was founded by a king, a count, a lord, an abbot or a bishop. Want to learn more about t
tldr: Flânez dans les ruelles médiévales de Sauveterre-de-Rouergue et admirez ses 47 arcades et ses maisons à colombages.

name: Explore St-Just-sur-Viaur
description:
The St-Just-sur-Viaur District had around 1,700 inhabitants in late 19th century. With the last-century rural exodus, woods replaced hemp growing, fruit trees and vineyards. Today, with some 230 inhabitants, it is an ideal choice for nature and old-stone lovers.
A village that has been around for quite some time...

First mentioned in 1241, this former fortified hamlet hosts beautiful buildings, like the priory overlooking the River Viaur. In the old days, it belonged to the nuns of the "Monastère-sous-Rodez" and, as most of the Church properties, it was put up to auction in 1793. Have a look
tldr: Découvrez un village marqué par l'exode rural, où la nature a repris ses droits sur les anciennes cultures.

name: Explore Taurines
description:
A hamlet built on a legend...


According to a local legend, it is said Taurines's primitive church was founded after a grave containing bones was discovered. Supposedly, its location was indicated by a bull's odd behaviour : it was scratching the ground at that precise spot (hence the name of "Taurines", bull meaning "taureau" in French). The population believed the bones belonged to holy body's remains, what was never confirmed by the Church.

... you can explore & unveil its heritage!
Take time to stroll in the hamlet & try to spot the Gallo-Roman altar or the castle's gate... that is no lo
tldr: Visitez un hameau bâti sur une légende locale, où une église aurait été fondée après la découverte d'ossements mystérieux.

Have a good experience !

description:
Nestled in the heart of a listed site on the Causse Noir, the Fed âne farm welcomes you with ?fèdes? (ewes), donkeys and many other furry and feathered animals. I'd be delighted to take you on a discovery tour or a longer adventure with one or more donkeys. An affectionate and hard-working companion, he'll accompany you between causses and rivers, and carry your belongings all the way!
Possibility of bivouacking on site and in surrounding farms (taking advantage of local produce) or staying in a gîte / auberge.
Sale of organic farm products: organic sheep meat products (dry sausage, terrines,
tldr: Randonnez avec des ânes sur le Causse Noir et découvrez un élevage familial au cœur d'un site classé.

name: Fenaille Museum
description: Museum conserving rich collections of archaeology, art and history. The museum is renowned for its exceptional ensemble of statue-menhirs - sculpted 5000 years ago, they are the oldest monumental statues known in western Europe. The museum's circuit retraces the history of the Rouergue from the first man (300000years ago) to the 17th century. It is organised around four main themes: the statue-menhirs, ancient Rodez, the Rouergue in the Middle Ages, the 16th century and the Renaissance. Numerous tools to help your visit and enable a personalised approach to the collections using models, drawin
tldr: Admirez des statues-menhirs vieilles de 5000 ans, parmi les plus anciennes sculptures monumentales d'Europe.

name: Fenassac, gîte à la ferme en Aveyron
description:
Why come to us?
We'd like to welcome you to our charming, flower-filled setting, in a simple, family atmosphere. We like to share and enjoy our time together, while respecting your peace and quiet, of course!
If you wish, you can try out some of the farm's activities with us: picking vegetables from the garden, collecting eggs... and you can even watch the calves feed at our daughter's farm nearby.
A basket of home-grown produce will be waiting for you on arrival to get your vacation off to a good start, and, if the garden is willing, you'll have vegetables throughout your stay.
A few details

description: Fer d'Aqui is a young company based in Onet le Château in Aveyron. We work with iron to create a wide range of staircases, balustrades and designer furniture. We have a 0-waste approach, so we try to recycle our production offcuts into objects designed by a local architect.
tldr: Explorez des escaliers et meubles design forgés à partir de matériaux recyclés dans un atelier local.

Creation of lightings in an industrial and design spirit.

Silhouettes with "flat heads" can be realized according to your desires and your ideas.
Open all year round
tldr: Découvrez des créations uniques en fer forgé, transformant objets anciens en luminaires et décorations originales.

name: Ferme Auberge de La Tindelle
description:
An old restored farmhouse with beautiful vaulted rooms welcomes you to discover the valley of the Tarn, the cherries, ewes and asparagus of the Causse.

It is in all conviviality that we welcome you in our farm lost on the black causse. Come and taste the products from our farm, the vegetables from our garden on the banks of the Tarn, the delicious fruit from the hillsides, the asparagus from the Causse Noir and of course the famous lambs from the Causse Noir that feast on the orchids. After the meal we recommend a digestive walk among the ruiniformes of the Causse in search of our pigs and sh
tldr: Savourez une cuisine locale à base de cerises, d'agneau et d'asperges dans une ferme restaurée aux voûtes anciennes.

name: Ferme Auberge La Ferme de Peyrouse

tldr: Goûtez des plats fermiers dans une ancienne étable, avec des produits issus de la ferme ou des voisins.

name: Ferme auberge La Grange de Séveyrac
description:
In an authentic setting of stone and wood, Anne and Jean-Yves Rieucau, both farmers, welcome you to La Grange de Séveyrac, a converted, heated or air-conditioned farm inn.

description: On the Causse Sauveterre, the hamlet of Monziols testifies to a long agricultural activity which still persists today. The breeding, associated with the cereal culture, shaped both the landscapes and the buildings. One of the farms offers a beautiful glimpse of this past: it is located slightly away from the hamlet. Organized around an inner courtyard, the buildings are made of limestone. The main facade is the most elaborate, with its high gallery opening onto the courtyard through five arcades, which serves the dwellings and the wings of the other buildings. tldr: Visitez un hameau caussenard où élevage et culture façonnent encore aujourd'hui un paysage préservé.

description:
As market gardeners specializing in herbs, we choose varieties for their flavor in cooking.
We practice chemical-free farming and encourage biological regulation in our crops.

Our dishes are prepared the same day using our own produce and that of local organic producers. We also prepare the condiments, herbs and spices you'll find in our dishes.
tldr: Dégustez des plats préparés avec des herbes aromatiques cultivées sans pesticides dans une ferme maraîchère.

The farm of Bouniols is a small organic farm where we have several activities. The main activity is the breeding of goats and the transformation of cheese. We also have laying hens, 4 donkeys and we produce vegetables. We make conserves (sweet and salty).

You can find us on the market of Saint-Affrique all year long and of Saint-Rome-de-Tarn in summer.

tldr: Plongez dans l'histoire d'une ferme ovine séculaire et vivez son quotidien au fil des saisons.
